correctness.rationale: A full A/B/edge-grid invariant decomposition yields the explicit 2-by-2 mass form and strictly negative complementary blocks for p<1. At the original biclique cutoff the zero-mass witness has zero energy but a nonzero mixed energy for unequal parts, proving strict earlier failure. The first mass-form zero has exactly one null direction and lower exponents have strict negative type; strict snowflake interpolation excludes any larger admissible exponent. Direct Taylor expansions of H give the fixed-m inverse-n constant. The extracted checker independently constructs distances by BFS and tests block formulas, centered inertia and asymptotic probes. The finite cases do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Adjoining all edge midpoints to a complete bipartite metric is an intrinsic natural metric operation. Balanced biclique negative type survives it, whereas unequal parts produce a strictly new mass-sector obstruction. The resulting all-parameter sharp cutoff and endpoint rank are complete, and the fixed-thin-side cutoff collapses as 1/n even though the original graph retains a positive limit. This discontinuous behavior across balance is structural and not a routine reparameterization.
